authorized_network.description:
The full name of the GCE network to connect the instance to.  If not provided,
'default' will be used.
authorized_network.rationale: Selecting the correct VPC network ensures that instances are accessed only from trusted networks, thereby improving data security.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

deletion_protection.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance.
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is not set to false in Terraform state.
When the field is set to true or unset in Terraform state, a 'terraform apply'
or 'terraform destroy' that would delete the instance will fail.
When the field is set to false, deleting the instance is allowed.

display_name.description: A user-visible name for the instance.
display_name.rationale: Human-readable name for the instance; it is cosmetic metadata and does not control access, encryption, or exposure.

labels.description:
Resource labels to represent user-provided metadata.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Key/value metadata labels for organisation and cost allocation; they do not affect access control or encryption, so they are not a policy target.

memcache_version.description:
The major version of Memcached software. If not provided, latest supported version will be used.
Currently the latest supported major version is MEMCACHE_1_5. The minor version will be automatically
determined by our system based on the latest supported minor version. Default value: "MEMCACHE_1_5" Possible values: ["MEMCACHE_1_5", "MEMCACHE_1_6_15"]
memcache_version.rationale: Sets the Memcached major version. Running an outdated version increases exposure to known vulnerabilities; a policy should require a supported/current minimum version so the instance stays patched.

name.description: The resource name of the instance.

node_count.description: Number of nodes in the memcache instance.
node_count.rationale: Number of nodes in the instance; it affects capacity and availability only and does not control access, encryption, or exposure.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

region.description: The region of the Memcache instance. If it is not provided, the provider region is used.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

reserved_ip_range_id.description:
Contains the name of allocated IP address ranges associated with
the private service access connection for example, "test-default"
associated with IP range 10.0.0.0/29.
reserved_ip_range_id.rationale: Names the pre-allocated private-service-access IP range the instance uses. It is a reference to an existing allocated range and only avoids addressing conflicts; it does not grant access or change network exposure, so it is not a useful policy target.

zones.description:
Zones where memcache nodes should be provisioned.  If not
provided, all zones will be used.
zones.rationale: Zones within the region where nodes are provisioned; zone selection within an already-approved region is an availability/placement choice and is not constrained here (region/data-residency is handled by the location whitelist).

maintenance_policy.description.description:
Optional. Description of what this policy is for.
Create/Update methods return INVALID_ARGUMENT if the
length is greater than 512.
maintenance_policy.description.rationale: Free-text description of the maintenance policy; it is human-readable metadata and does not control any security behaviour.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description:
Required. Maintenance window that is applied to resources covered by this policy.
Minimum 1. For the current version, the maximum number of weekly_maintenance_windows
is expected to be one.

Required. The day of week that maintenance updates occur.
- DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED: The day of the week is unspecified.
- MONDAY: Monday
- TUESDAY: Tuesday
- WEDNESDAY: Wednesday
- THURSDAY: Thursday
- FRIDAY: Friday
- SATURDAY: Saturday
- SUNDAY: Sunday Possible values: ["DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED", "MONDAY", "TUESDAY", "WEDNESDAY", "THURSDAY", "FRIDAY", "SATURDAY", "SUNDAY"]
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Selecting an appropriate day ensures maintenance does not disrupt peak traffic periods.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description:
Required. The length of the maintenance window, ranging from 3 hours to 8 hours.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits,
terminated by 's'. Example: "3.5s".
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Specifying the duration ensures that updates are completed within a controlled timeframe.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description: Required. Start time of the window in UTC time.

Hours of day in 24 hour format. Should be from 0 to 23.
An API may choose to allow the value "24:00:00" for scenarios like business closing time.
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Correct hour selection ensures updates align with expected downtime periods.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description: Minutes of hour of day. Must be from 0 to 59.
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Precise minute specification helps align maintenance with exact scheduling needs.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description: Fractions of seconds in nanoseconds. Must be from 0 to 999,999,999.
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Nanosecond precision is rarely required for maintenance windows but ensures full compatibility with GCP TimeOfDay format.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description:
Seconds of minutes of the time. Must normally be from 0 to 59.
An API may allow the value 60 if it allows leap-seconds.
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Seconds allow fine-grained control of the start time, but usually default to 0.

memcache_parameters.description: User-specified parameters for this memcache instance.

memcache_parameters.params.description: User-defined set of parameters to use in the memcache process.

node_config.cpu_count.rationale: Number of vCPUs per Memcache node; it affects capacity and cost only and does not control access, encryption, or network exposure.

node_config.memory_size_mb.description: Memory size in Mebibytes for each memcache node.
node_config.memory_size_mb.rationale: RAM per Memcache node; it affects capacity and cost only and does not control access, encryption, or exposure.
